messages:
maya: Heads-up — console alerted a spike in fncall validation rejects for several routes. :warning:
leo: saw it too, looks like a bunch of tool responses suddenly started returning arrays where we expect objects.
priya: confirmed on sampling. Example from logs:```json
{
  "error": "validation_failed",
  "path": "response.result",
  "expected": "object",
  "received": "array"
}
```
sam: any recent rollouts touching tool adapter or coercion logic?
maya: rolled a permissive adapter tweak yesterday evening to 10% canary for better backwards compatibility. Maybe that change interacted poorly with strict validators upstream.
leo: that canary should only increase permissive accepts, not flip arrays into being emitted. Could be client-side change in adapter mapping layer.
priya: telemetry shows reject-rate correlated with account shard us-west-2 and model-variant v3b. Can we route a few of those through the legacy shim to validate? @devex
devex: yep I can flip a routing rule for a 5% slice to the legacy shim. Will instrument additional tags for sampling.
infra-bot: action created: INFRA-1209 — create temporary route to legacy-tool-adapter for shard us-west-2 (owner: devex)
sam: what about billing/quota impact? rejects can cause retries and extra token cost. We should map rejected toolcalls to a degen fallback only after N attempts.
leo: agree. Short term: devex route + increase sampling for telemetry (keep raw payloads for 30m) so we can reproduce. Medium term: change validator to emit a soft warning + fallback rather than hard reject when top-level tuple/array shapes are seen.
priya: dashboard query I used: `sum(rate(fncall.validation.rejects[5m])) by (route, model_variant)` — shows a 4x bump at 02:13 UTC.
maya: can someone paste a sanitized raw payload for one of the failures? Might reveal if adapter wrapped an object in an array.
devex: pasted one into #eng-platform-log-samples. TL;DR: tool returns `[ { "id": 42, "result": {...} } ]` but our callsite expects `{ "id": 42, "result": {...} }`.
leo: that explains it. Two options: adapter should coerce single-item arrays into the singular object (heuristic), or validator should accept single-item arrays as equivalent for a migration window.
sam: leaning toward validator soft-accept with a structured flag so billing/console shows these as "coercion-accepted" vs "strict-reject". That keeps audit trail.
maya: agree. Let's implement a temporary soft-accept path gated by a feature-flag per-route. We can backfill telemetry and use the console to bubble up the new metric: `fncall.coercion.accepted`
priya: will update the dashboard tiles and add an alert threshold (if coercion-accepted > 10% of total fncalls for > 15m).
devex: toggled the legacy route for 5% at 1704123468. Observability tags: `coercion_handoff=legacy_shim`, `sample=true`.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary traffic rule applied to route /v1/fncall for shard us-west-2 (5%).
leo: next actions: (1) devex - keep route and collect 30m of raw samples; (2) eng-platform (maya & sam) - implement soft-accept flag + metric `fncall.coercion.accepted`; (3) priya - dashboard + alert; (4) devex - coordinate rollback if errors increase.
maya: I'll draft the PR for soft-accept; will include unit tests for single-item array coercion and explicit opt-out config.
sam: thanks. One more note — make sure billing tags still reflect attempted strict call so we don't undercount rejects for invoices.
leo: good catch. Add `billing.tag=attempted_strict` when coercion path flips on.
priya: adding that to dashboard mapping.
maya: OK, I'll open PR and tag reviewers. Removing broad strict rollouts until this is reconciled. :thumbsup:
